data.title: Bot Traffic Behavioral Anomaly — Mechanical Consistency in Affiliate Session Metrics
data.description: Detects bot-generated affiliate traffic by identifying sessions with mechanical behavioral consistency — identical session durations, linear scroll patterns, and zero mouse movement variance — that indicate automated rather than human browsing. Bot networks account for approximately 40% of all click fraud, and AI-powered bots increasingly mimic individual human sessions. However, bot traffic still exhibits statistically detectable patterns at the population level: genuine human traffic has natural variance in behavioral metrics, while bot traffic — even sophisticated AI bots — produces distributions with anomalously low standard deviation. This rule analyzes session-level behavioral distributions per affiliate to detect mechanical consistency at the aggregate level.

detection.condition: selection AND filter_volume AND (filter_mechanical OR filter_scroll OR filter_mouse)

enrichment_required.source: Standard deviation of session durations per affiliate over timeframe
Standard deviation of scroll depth per affiliate over timeframe
Ratio of sessions with zero mouse movement to total sessions per affiliate

queries.sql:
-- SQL: Bot Traffic Behavioral Anomaly Detection
-- Affiliate traffic with mechanical consistency indicating automated activity
SELECT
  a.affiliate_id,
  a.affiliate_name,
  COUNT(*) AS session_count,
  ROUND(AVG(s.session_duration_sec), 2) AS avg_session_duration,
  ROUND(STDDEV(s.session_duration_sec), 2) AS session_duration_stddev,
  ROUND(AVG(s.scroll_depth_pct), 2) AS avg_scroll_depth,
  ROUND(STDDEV(s.scroll_depth_pct), 2) AS scroll_depth_stddev,
  ROUND(AVG(s.mouse_movement_pixels), 2) AS avg_mouse_movement,
  ROUND(STDDEV(s.mouse_movement_pixels), 2) AS mouse_movement_stddev,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN s.mouse_movement_pixels = 0 THEN 1 END) AS zero_mouse_sessions,
  ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN s.mouse_movement_pixels = 0 THEN 1 END) * 1.0
        / COUNT(*), 3) AS zero_mouse_ratio,
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.src_ip) AS distinct_ips,
  ROUND(AVG(s.page_views), 2) AS avg_page_views
FROM affiliate_sessions s
JOIN affiliates a ON s.affiliate_id = a.affiliate_id
WHERE s.session_date >= DATEADD(DAY, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
  AND s.traffic_source = 'affiliate'
GROUP BY a.affiliate_id, a.affiliate_name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100
  AND (STDDEV(s.session_duration_sec) < 1.0
       OR STDDEV(s.scroll_depth_pct) < 2.0
       OR (COUNT(CASE WHEN s.mouse_movement_pixels = 0 THEN 1 END) * 1.0
           / COUNT(*)) > 0.5)
ORDER BY session_count DESC
queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL: Bot Traffic Behavioral Anomaly Detection")`
`comment("Detects mechanical consistency in affiliate session behavioral metrics")`
index=flame_advertising sourcetype=flame:web_analytics
  traffic_source="affiliate"
| stats count AS session_count,
        avg(session_duration_sec) AS avg_duration,
        stdev(session_duration_sec) AS duration_stddev,
        avg(scroll_depth_pct) AS avg_scroll,
        stdev(scroll_depth_pct) AS scroll_stddev,
        avg(mouse_movement_pixels) AS avg_mouse,
        stdev(mouse_movement_pixels) AS mouse_stddev,
        sum(if(mouse_movement_pixels=0, 1, 0)) AS zero_mouse_sessions,
        dc(src_ip) AS distinct_ips
  BY affiliate_id, affiliate_name
| where session_count >= 100
  AND (duration_stddev < 1.0 OR scroll_stddev < 2.0
       OR (zero_mouse_sessions / session_count) > 0.5)
| sort - session_count
queries.cql:
// CrowdStrike CQL: Bot Traffic Behavioral Anomaly
// Mechanical consistency in affiliate session metrics
traffic_source="affiliate"
| groupBy(affiliate_id, function=[
    count(as=session_count),
    avg(field=session_duration_sec, as=avg_duration),
    stddev(field=session_duration_sec, as=duration_stddev),
    avg(field=scroll_depth_pct, as=avg_scroll),
    stddev(field=scroll_depth_pct, as=scroll_stddev),
    avg(field=mouse_movement_pixels, as=avg_mouse),
    stddev(field=mouse_movement_pixels, as=mouse_stddev)
  ])
| session_count >= 100
| duration_stddev < 1.0 OR scroll_stddev < 2.0
| sort(session_count, order=desc)

references: Anura, Invalid Traffic Report 2025 — 40% bot traffic
TrafficGuard, Ad Fraud Report 2025 — bot network analysis
Tapper, Affiliate Fraud Trends 2026 — AI bot evolution
Juniper Research, Ad Fraud Market Analysis 2025 — USD 71B projection
falsepositives: Legitimate automated testing or monitoring tools generating uniform traffic patterns
Accessibility tools that produce consistent browsing patterns (screen readers, keyboard-only navigation)
Embedded browser views in mobile apps with constrained interaction patterns
